newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends down, off lows, after tracking US.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends down, off lows, after tracking US.

text.p: IPE gas oil closed $2 a tonne lower on Monday, but off earlier lows as NYMEX gasoline led a modest recovery, dealers said.
"Gasoline has been the leader today," said one dealer.
Feb gas oil, which expires on Wednesday, closed $2 lower at $188.25 a tonne, having dipped to a session low of $186.25. March shed $4, widening the front month backwardation to $7 a tonne.
NYMEX gasoline fell sharply shortly after its open, shedding over 1.5 cents to a low of 61.40 cents a gallon, before staging a partial recovery to trade at 62.40 cents a gallon at 1745 GMT.
Traders said that gasoline was bearing the brunt of heavy fund selling on NYMEX.
Dealers expected U.S. gasoline imports to approach historically high levels of some 650,000 barrels per day in February due in part to an open arbitrage from Europe in January.
"NYMEX was sold heavily by the funds on Friday and they've come back again," said one dealer.
IPE Brent was also seen tracking U.S. markets. The March contract tumbled to a low of $20.55 a barrel in mid-afternoon, having crashed through several support levels.
March Brent was trading 25 cents down at $20.70 at 1800 GMT.
"We were following the U.S. but volumes weren't as heavy here," said one IPE dealer.
Earlier, Brent made an unsustained upside break in a technical correction to Friday's sharp selloff which saw the spot contract slide below $21 for the first time since August.
